function: Channel estimation in RIS-assisted ISAC: CGAN estimates the cascaded BS-RIS-UE communication channel at each user and the BS-target-BS sensing channel at the BS from pilots (pp. 4, 11)
system: RIS-assisted MISO ISAC: full-duplex BS with M=4 antennas, K=3 single-antenna users, reflecting RIS with N=30 elements, direct link blocked, narrowband; carrier frequency not stated (pp. 5-7, 20)
method: Conditional GAN, supervised adversarial training with an added L2 term: feedforward SE-CGAN (sensing) and CNN CE-CGAN (communication); generator conditioned on received signals; offline training (pp. 11-15)
data_channel: Own simulator: radar model for BS-target-BS, Rician (K=10) BS-RIS and Rayleigh RIS-UE links, path loss exponents 3, 2.3, 2; 10^4 samples per SNR, 90/10 train/test (pp. 20-21)
test_conditions: Trained at SNR 10, 15, 20 dB, M=4, N=30; tested on held-out 10% at SNR -10 to 30 dB; M 4-16 and N 20-50 also varied, retraining not stated (pp. 21-26)
baselines: Learned only: benchmark DNN estimator [20], feedforward network (FFN), extreme learning machine (ELM); no classical estimator such as LS is compared (pp. 21-22)
metrics: NMSE of the communication and sensing channels versus SNR, M and N; complexity as real additions and multiplications and its reduction over the benchmark (pp. 21-27)
complexity: Real additions and multiplications derived in closed form (Eqs. 28-42) and plotted versus M and N; SE-CGAN cheaper than benchmark [20], CE-CGAN comparable (pp. 16-19, 26-27)
openness: none; no link to code or data and no release statement in the paper
q1_support: p. 20: "The sensing channel is modeled according to the radar channel model as". Communication channels are Rician (K = 10) for BS-RIS and Rayleigh for RIS-UE with own path loss exponents (p. 21); no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 21: "The choice of the SNR region ensures that the model encounters instances". Only the SNR differs between training (10, 15, 20 dB) and testing (-10 to 30 dB), an SNR sweep; Table I (p. 18) sizes the networks with M and N, and the paper never says a trained model is tested on another configuration.
q3_support: p. 22: "FF network (FFN) and extreme learning machine (ELM)." The compared methods are the DNN benchmark [20], FFN and ELM, all learned; least squares appears only in the related work (p. 4) and no non-learned estimator is compared in Figs. 3-6.
q4_support: p. 16: "The computational complexity is computed in terms of the number of real". Additions and multiplications of the proposed networks are derived (Eqs. 28-42) and plotted against the benchmark in Fig. 7 (p. 27).
q5_support: p. 21: "90% of the dataset size is used for training". The data are generated by the authors' own simulator; the paper gives no link to code or data, uses no public dataset and makes no release statement.
notes: The PDF is the arXiv v1 (24 Feb 2025) of the CGAN paper; p. 1 shows only a DOI placeholder (TCOMM.2025.xxxxxxx), so the match rests on the title and topic. Area 2: channel estimation in an ISAC system. q3 is 0 because every compared method is learned. q2 is 0 because the SNR range test is an SNR sweep and the paper does not state testing in another configuration; the reviewer may check the M and N sweeps (pp. 23-26), where the model is said to be optimized for M = 4 and N = 30.
